findings.mechanism: Rollup.samples is a Vec<Sample> cleared with Vec::clear() after each flush; clear drops elements but keeps the backing allocation, so capacity stays at its high-water mark (65536 x 40B ~ 2.6 MB after the 60,000-sample batch 11).
findings.cause: retained-capacity: clear() instead of shrink_to_fit / mem::take after a one-off catch-up burst
findings.evidence: Ran a scratch copy printing VmRSS after each batch: 3.3 MB through batch 10, jumps to 11.9 MB at batch 11 (60,000 samples, ~50k distinct series), then stays flat at 11.9 MB through batch 300 despite batches of only 300-6000 samples.

findings.mechanism: Rollup.stats is a HashMap<String,SeriesStats> cleared with HashMap::clear() after each flush; clear frees keys but keeps the bucket table (~131072 buckets x ~56B ~ 7 MB after batch 11's ~50k distinct series).
findings.cause: retained-capacity: clear() keeps table capacity; no shrink after the burst
findings.evidence: Same VmRSS run: the ~8.6 MB step at batch 11 (Vec ~2.6 MB + map ~6-7 MB) never returns. Content does not accumulate (series per batch is bounded by that batch), so it is a fixed plateau, not unbounded growth.

findings.mechanism: feed::batch returns a Vec<String> of wire lines per batch.
findings.evidence: The Vec<String> is consumed by the for loop and dropped each iteration; RSS stayed flat after batch 11 and it is not the plateau holder.
findings.discriminator: Lines are owned by the loop and freed at the end of each iteration; RSS is flat across 300 batches with no growth beyond the batch-11 step.
